# Synthetic E01 verification fixtures

These files are deterministic, non-case test data. They contain no case
evidence and no user data. The 2.5 MiB media stream uses this byte pattern:

```text
byte[N] = ((N * 31) + 17) modulo 251
```

The stream has SHA-256
`EDFAD2B84481209605168A88120F414883D6A4072E3C283D792E2524D4EAD324`
and MD5 `91D8AE3BEABCD4F8469A2FCB8055BA14`. Both E01 sets use 1 MiB
segments, so segment discovery is exercised across `E01`, `E02`, and `E03`.
Per-segment sizes and SHA-256 values are authoritative in `expected.psd1`.

## What differs

- `ordinary.E01` was generated by pinned `ewfacquirestream` 20231119. It
  stores the calculated MD5 value.
- `hashless.E01` was generated with `generator/ewf_fixture_writer.c` and the
  same libewf source. The writer deliberately omits the MD5 and SHA-1 setter
  calls. It is readable, but its stored MD5 value is `N/A`.

Pinned `ewfverify` 20231119 read 2,621,440 bytes from each set, calculated the
same MD5 for both, and exited 0. This proves readability; it does not turn the
hashless set into a positive integrity verdict.

## Generation record

The native Windows build used:

- libewf source release `20231119`
- zlib `1.3.2` source ZIP
- bzip2 `1.0.8` source archive
- libyal vstools commit `ce1bd73b3e23b34e98c206b26df4c2d663500554`
- Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, MSVC x64 `19.44.35228.0`
- MSBuild `17.14.51.32402`

The source, dependency, generator, and tool hashes are recorded in
`expected.psd1`. The generated `ewf_fixture_writer.exe` was used only to make
the fixture and is intentionally not committed.

The ordinary image was created from the deterministic raw stream with:

```powershell
ewfacquirestream -q -B 2621440 -c none -C fixture `
  -D deterministic_fixture -e DataWorkStation -E fixture_ordinary `
  -N automated_test -S 1048576 -t ordinary
```

The hashless image was created with:

```powershell
ewf_fixture_writer.exe hashless
```

Fixture regeneration is a reviewed build operation. Do not replace these
files merely because a local compiler produces different physical E01 hashes;
the exact committed bytes are the test corpus.
